title: Add CI smoke tests for streaming + tool-calling + retrieval (flake-mitigated)
author: Sabrina James
release_notes: Adds CI smoke coverage to catch common regressions in template apps: streaming disconnect handling, tool-call parsing/validation, and retrieval returning empty context. Includes flake mitigation (timeouts, retries, and fork-safe skipping).
description: Title: Add CI smoke tests for streaming + tool-calling + retrieval (flake-mitigated) Summary: This PR adds a small, gated smoke-test suite for the RAG+agent quickstarts (Python + TypeScript) to catch the failure modes we keep seeing in internal beta and support: (1) streaming disconnects / partial chunks; (2) tool-call parsing and schema validation regressions; (3) retrieval pipelines returning empty context due to chunking/indexing drift. The goal is not to run a full eval in CI, but to fail fast when we break the “happy path” scaffolding. What’s included: - Python smoke tests (pytest) covering: streaming response completes without raising + yields at least N chunks; a tool-call roundtrip produces a valid, schema-conformant tool invocation; retrieval returns at least 1 document chunk for a seeded mini-corpus and the agent includes citations in the final answer. - TypeScript smoke tests (vitest) covering: server-side streaming handler tolerates a forced reconnect (simulated via a short-lived proxy) without hanging; tool-call JSON parsing returns actionable errors on invalid tool payloads; retrieval adapter returns non-empty results for the same seeded corpus. - A CI job that runs smoke tests only when secrets are available (skips on forks) and caps cost/latency by pinning small prompts, max_tokens, and concurrency. - Flake mitigation notes + implementation: increased read timeouts for streaming tests, bounded retries around known-transient network errors, and hard test-level deadlines to prevent CI hangs. Flake mitigation details: - Streaming tests are the most sensitive to runner/network variance. We do not assert token-by-token content; we assert: (a) stream starts within a deadline; (b) at least one chunk is received; (c) the stream terminates cleanly (finish_reason or EOF) within a max duration; (d) we log request_id and reconnect attempts for debugging. - Retries are limited and only applied to retryable classes (connection reset, transient 502/503, gateway timeouts). Any auth/quota/tool-schema errors fail immediately (non-retryable). - Tests are forced to low cost: max_tokens <= 64, temperature=0, single request per test file, and a dedicated CI model configured via RW_SMOKE_MODEL. CI wiring: - Adds a dedicated workflow job `smoke-quickstarts` that runs on pull_request and main, but will no-op if REDWOOD_API_KEY is not present (fork-safe). - The job prints a short “what to do if this fails” section including: request_id lookup, toggling RW_LOG_LEVEL=debug, and how to re-run locally via `./scripts/smoke/run_smoke.sh`. Why: This is directly aligned with ENG-4186 and addresses regressions that have shown up in SUP-29410 (streaming disconnects behind certain proxies) and SUP-29441 (tool schema parse errors). It should also reduce churn in template review since it makes “streaming/tooling/retrieval still works” a check rather than a manual run. Rollout: - Gate as required for template PRs touching streaming/tooling/retrieval code. - Keep it intentionally small; deeper correctness stays in the eval harness. - If flake rate > 1% over a week, we’ll move the streaming reconnect simulation to nightly only and keep the basic streaming completion check on PRs.
commits: ci: add smoke job and fork-safe skipping
python(smoke): add streaming completion + request_id logging assertions
python(smoke): add tool-call schema validation test + non-retryable error handling
python(smoke): add retrieval mini-corpus seed + non-empty context assertion
ts(smoke): add streaming handler smoke test with deadline + reconnect simulation
ts(smoke): add tool-call parse/validation smoke test
docs: add local rerun instructions and flake mitigation notes
conversation: Sahana Iyer (review): The job looks good but please make sure it doesn’t run on forks (no secrets). Also can we guarantee it won’t hang the runner if streaming stalls? Add a hard per-test deadline and ensure the workflow has a max timeout.

Sabrina James (author): Added fork-safe `if: secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY != ''` guard + 20m job timeout. Also added per-test deadline (pytest timeout + vitest testTimeout) and explicit stream read max duration so we fail fast instead of hanging.

Dana Lo (review): Tool smoke should cover the “invalid tool args shape” case we hit last week. Right now it only tests the happy path. Can you add one negative test to ensure the error message points to the tool name + JSON path?

Sabrina James (author): Added `test_tool_call_invalid_args_shape` in both Python and TS. It asserts we surface: tool name, validation error, and a stable error code so the README troubleshooting can link to it.
Ibrahim Khan (review): Re: retries—please do not retry on 4xx or tool schema failures. Also avoid token-by-token assertions in streaming; we should only assert stream completes and yields chunks.
Sabrina James (author): Updated retry wrapper to only retry on retryable network/5xx. Streaming test now asserts start/chunk/finish with deadlines; removed content assertions.
Christine Wong (review): Please add request_id logging to help support correlate failures, and ensure the seeded corpus doesn’t contain anything that might be mistaken for PII.
Sabrina James (author): Logging now prints `redwood_request_id` and trace id (if present) on failure. Mini corpus is synthetic product docs; no personal data. Added a comment + README note.
Monica Patel (approve): This is the right level of coverage for PR gating. Let’s keep the reconnect simulation behind an env flag if we see flake, but ship as-is for a week to measure.
Sahana Iyer (approve): ✅ Approved after timeout/deadline changes. Please monitor flake rate; if we see retries hiding real issues, we can tighten the retryable set.
post_merge_notes: Action item: Sahana to add a weekly flake-rate report for `smoke-quickstarts` (by workflow run) and revisit whether reconnect simulation should be PR-gated or nightly-only.
